Iconoclast

eye-KAH-nuh-klast · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Iconoclast is a person who attacks or challenges cherished beliefs, traditions, or institutions.

Long before he became famous, the composer was dismissed by critics as a reckless iconoclast with no respect for tradition.

Worked Example

The teenage chess prodigy became known as an iconoclast for openly mocking decades-old opening strategies that every grandmaster had once treated as untouchable.

The chess player wasn't just disagreeing quietly -- she was publicly attacking ideas that everyone else treated as sacred, which is exactly what makes someone an iconoclast.

How Iconoclast Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

maverick

maverick: someone who thinks and acts independently, against convention

rebel

rebel: someone who resists or defies established authority or ideas

Antonyms

traditionalist

traditionalist: someone who strongly supports established customs and beliefs

conformist

conformist: someone who follows accepted norms and behavior

How Strong Is It? — critic → iconoclast → revolutionary

critic vs. iconoclast

critic vs. iconoclast: A critic simply points out flaws or offers judgment, a much quieter stance than actively attacking cherished beliefs.

revolutionary vs. iconoclast

revolutionary vs. iconoclast: A revolutionary doesn't just challenge beliefs -- they try to completely overthrow the entire system built on them.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of iconoclast.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — icon (eikon)

root — icon (eikon): image, likeness -- especially a sacred or revered image (Greek)

suffix — -oclast (klastes)

suffix — -oclast (klastes): breaker (Greek)

Put it together

Put it together: Iconoclast comes from Greek eikon ('image') + klastes ('breaker') -- literally an 'image-breaker.' It first described people who destroyed religious icons, then came to mean anyone who attacks cherished, traditional beliefs.

Use the root in a new word: icon

Use the root in a new word: icon: The old cathedral displayed a golden icon of the city's patron saint above the altar.

Root Check

Word Choice

Iconoclast is almost always used with a hint of admiration or boldness -- it describes someone breaking with tradition on purpose, not someone who is simply careless or ignorant of it.
